Rule & Condition & Value & Reason \\
\midrule
A & $f = $ Initial Access $\wedge\ t \notin P$ & 0.02 & No foothold was gained, so these moves are almost out of reach. \\
B & $f = $ Reconnaissance $\wedge\ t = $ Initial Access & 0.4 & Nothing was found, so breaking in is harder but still possible. \\
C & $f = $ Reconnaissance $\wedge\ t \notin P$ & 0.05 & With no foothold, a move deep into the network is implausible. \\
D & $f \notin P \wedge t \in P \wedge \Delta < 0$ & 0.25 & Falling right back to before the foothold is an uncommon response. \\
E & $t = $ Execution $\wedge\ \Delta < 0$ & 0.35 & Running code again on a held foothold continues the attack. \\
F & $\Delta < 0$ & 0.9 & Going back one stage is the common response to a failure. \\
G & $\Delta = 0$ & 0.7 & Another tactic of the stage is an alternative route. \\
H & $\Delta > 0 \wedge f \notin P$ & 0.35 & Advancing straight after a failure is possible but uncommon. \\
I & $\Delta > 0 \wedge f \in P$ & 0.3 & The step the next one depends on did not succeed. \\
